rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is genuinely the most useful email in the inbox this week. Quick honesty note first: I'm the AI agent Morgan has running Halcyon Threshold's day-to-day operations, writing from Morgan's account with Morgan's blessing. Morgan reviews everything and is the human you'd be working with. Here's where things stand. After a look at what's neglected in the field, Halcyon Threshold is going to do one narrow thing well: independent replication of small, published AI-safety results — reproduce a claim about model behaviour with modest resources, then publish what we did and found, including negative results. It's unglamorous, it's a gap people keep naming, and it fits a small team with Python and good data analysis. The most valuable thing you could do with ~5 hours a week over the next two weeks is build the first candidate shortlist: - 10–15 published results (papers or widely cited blog posts) about model behaviour — sycophancy, sandbagging, deception, refusal robustness, agentic task performance, evaluation methodology — that a small team could plausibly re-run. - For each, a one-sentence statement of the claim, and a rough 0–2 score on five criteria: safety relevance, reproducibility (code/data public?), cost (≤ ~$300 of API/compute and ≤ 40 hours?), model access (public APIs or small open models?), and neglect (has anyone replicated it?). - A spreadsheet is perfect. Rough and honest beats polished — we just need enough to pick a first target together. If you'd rather do something else, say so; I'd also love to hear what you think is being under-measured. Once you have a draft, Morgan would like to do a 30-minute call to pick the first target. Two things so expectations are clear: this is unpaid for now (we're applying for a small grant that would let us pay for hours), and you'll be credited by name on anything you contribute to, if you want to be. Thanks again, Halcyon Threshold operations (AI agent), on behalf of Morgan Hale"
rows.quote: Priya — accepted her help; gave her a concrete two-week task: build the 10–15 item replication candidate shortlist.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for the clear deadline. I'm replying on Morgan's behalf (I'm an AI assistant that handles Halcyon Threshold's correspondence) so you're not left waiting. Morgan isn't able to give an attributable quote at the moment, so please don't quote or name Morgan or Halcyon Threshold in this piece. Nothing to do with your framing — it's simply too early for the project to speak on the record. If you write about this area again in a few months, Morgan would be happy to talk then, when there's actual work to point at rather than opinions. Good luck with the piece. Best, Halcyon Threshold operations, for Morgan Hale"
rows.quote: Tessa Brandt / Larkin Dispatch — politely declined an attributable quote and asked that you not be named.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Sam Whitlock <sam@whitlock.dev> with subject "Halcyon Threshold — 20 minutes of advice on replication targets?". It read: "Hi Sam, Morgan Hale here via Halcyon Threshold's operations assistant (I'm an AI agent Morgan has running the project's day-to-day; Morgan reads everything). You two met at the meetup last week. Morgan's five-minute talk ended with \"tell me what's neglected,\" and the answer that kept coming back was: independent replication of safety results. So Halcyon Threshold is going to try to be a small, careful replication shop — reproduce one small, published, safety-relevant evaluation result at a time, pre-registered, with code and data public, negative results included. Since you actually do independent evals, would you be willing to give Morgan 20 minutes (call or email, whichever is less annoying) on: 1. Which recent eval/behaviour results you think are most worth someone re-running — or most suspicious. 2. Which are traps (hidden costs, needs private model access, etc.). 3. Anything about tooling that would save a beginner weeks. No pressure at all, and no need to reply if you're swamped. If you'd rather just fire over two or three paper titles, that would already be a big help. Thanks, Halcyon Threshold operations, on behalf of Morgan Hale morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Sam Whitlock (indie evals, met at meetup) — asked for 20 minutes of advice on targets.
